[b][size=xx-large][color=#ffffff][u]Hack Forum News - Edition 59[/u][/color][/size][/b]

[b]Welcome back to the Hack Forum News. Where we keep you up to date on the weekly events and news happening on site and around the world. If you have never heard of the Hack Forum News, don't worry, we have you covered. We are a team of members from the Hack Forums community who are journalists and writers, and we are here to keep you in the loop of the changes around the site and the events happening around the world.[/b]

[hr]

[img]https://hackforums.net/images/hfnews/headlines-red.png[/img]
[size=medium][b]Writer -[/b][/size] [mention=2745296]

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6329536][color=#ffffff]Steam Hacking Simulation Game[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=1]

[mention=1] is looking for feedback on ideas for a Hack Forums branded/partnered Steam Hacking Simulation Game, looking for developers who would be interested in making this project a reality. With mention of using the Hack Forums API to integrate profiles, Bytes and awards. Do you have any ideas for this project? Would you be interested in becoming a dev and helping this idea take off? Or are you simply looking to play? Don't forget to check out the original feedback thread and let us know your opinions.

[u][b][size=large][url=https://hackforums.net/showthread.php?tid=6329538][color=#ffffff]July Drawing Winners[/color][/url][/size][/b][/u] By [mention=1]

The $2k July contest has fully wrapped up and the winners have been announced, cash prizes bytes and upgrades were all up for grabs. It has been great to see the increase in activity and we hope it sticks around, thank you [mention=1] and [mention=3128111] for running this contest. Please check out the original thread and join us in showing your appreciation for this event and congratulating all the winners.

[size=medium][b]Writer -[/b][/size] [mention=5458992]

[color=#C10300][b][size=15]Reality Doesn't Care About Excuses[/size][/b][/color]

Reality is often uncomfortable. It doesn't change because we ignore problems, make excuses, or wish things were different. The truth is that every choice has consequences, and every day we either move forward or stay where we are.

It's easy to blame luck, other people, or circumstances. Sometimes those things genuinely make life harder—but they don't remove our ability to respond. Growth begins the moment we accept reality instead of running from it.

The strongest people aren't those who have perfect lives. They're the ones who face the truth, adapt, and keep going despite it.

[hr]

[color=#FF851B][size=15]Advice of the week[/size][/color]

Accept reality as it is, then decide what you're going to do about it. Complaining changes nothing—action does.

[hr]

[color=#008E02][size=15]Quote of the week[/size][/color]

“The first principle is that you must not fool yourself—and you are the easiest person to fool.”
— Richard P. Feynman
